blocks.title: At a community centre in Laval
blocks.context: Sofia wants to sign up for a French class. Olivier works at the reception desk.

lines.fr: Bonjour, madame. Vous avez besoin d'aide ?
lines.en: Hello, ma'am. Do you need help?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Oui, merci. J'ai besoin d'un formulaire pour le cours de français.
lines.en: Yes, thank you. I need a form for the French class.

lines.speaker: Olivier
lines.en: Here you are. What's your name?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Sofia Hernández. H-E-R-N-A-N-D-E-Z, avec un accent aigu sur le a.
lines.en: Sofia Hernández. H-E-R-N-A-N-D-E-Z, with an acute accent on the a.

blocks.body: Everything in this conversation comes from Units 1 to 3: greetings, spelling, [[s'appeler]], [[être]], [[habiter]], numbers, days and times. The only new verb is [[avoir]] (to have): [[vous avez]], [[j'ai]].

blocks.title: Avoir means “to have”
blocks.body:
[[Avoir]] is the second most important verb in French, after [[être]]. Like être, it is **irregular**, so learn its six forms as sound chunks.

Notice the **élision** (from Unit 1): [[je]] + [[ai]] → [[j'ai]]. And notice the **liaisons**: [[nous‿avons]], [[vous‿avez]], [[ils‿ont]], [[elles‿ont]], all with a *z* sound.

blocks.title: Avoir in the present
head: avoir
English
rows: you have (formal, or more than one person)
blocks.note: [[as]] and [[a]] sound the same. [[ai]] sounds like *é*.

blocks.title: Age: avoir, not être
blocks.note: In English you **are** 32. In French you **have** 32 years: [[J'ai trente-deux ans]]. Never forget the word [[ans]].

examples.en: How old are you? (to a friend)

examples.fr: Karim a vingt et un ans.

blocks.title: Saying what you need
blocks.note: [[Avoir besoin de]] means *to need* (literally “to have need of”). [[De]] becomes [[d']] before a vowel, so [[de un]] → [[d'un]], [[de une]] → [[d'une]].

blocks.title: Phone numbers and appointments
blocks.pattern: avoir + un numéro de téléphone / un rendez-vous
blocks.note: Avoir also works like English *have* for things you have: a phone number, an appointment, a class.

examples.fr: Vous avez un numéro de téléphone ?
examples.en: Do you have a phone number?

examples.fr: J'ai un numéro de téléphone canadien.
examples.en: I have a Canadian phone number.

examples.fr: Tu as un rendez-vous à quelle heure ?

blocks.title: Ils sont or ils ont?
blocks.body:
These two are easy to confuse, and they mean different things:

- [[ils sont]] (they **are**): you hear an **s** sound, “eel-son”.
- [[ils ont]] (they **have**): you hear a **z** sound, “eel-z-on”.

Age also brings back the liaisons from this unit: [[un an]] “u-n-an”, [[deux ans]] “duh-z-an”, [[six ans]] “see-z-an”, [[dix ans]] “dee-z-an”, [[vingt ans]] “van-t-an”, and [[neuf ans]] “nuh-v-an”.

examples.en: They are twenty (they have twenty years).

blocks.body:
- **Je suis 32 ans:** the most common mistake for English speakers. Say [[J'ai trente-deux ans]].
- **Forgetting ans:** [[J'ai trente-deux]] alone sounds incomplete. Add [[ans]].
- **Je ai:** always [[j'ai]].
- **Forgetting de:** not [[J'ai besoin un formulaire]], but [[J'ai besoin d'un formulaire]].
- **Être for nationality, avoir for age:** [[Je suis mexicaine. J'ai trente-quatre ans.]]

blocks.title: Avoir where English uses “be”
blocks.body:
Age is not the only case. French uses [[avoir]] for several states where English uses *to be*. You will meet them later, but recognize them now:

- [[avoir faim]] = to be hungry (to have hunger)
- [[avoir soif]] = to be thirsty
- [[avoir froid]] / [[avoir chaud]] = to be cold / hot

So if you say [[Je suis froid]], a French speaker hears something like “I am a cold person”! Say [[J'ai froid]].

blocks.title: Filling in forms in Canada
blocks.body:
Forms in Québec and French-speaking Canada often use these words:

- [[Nom]] = last name, [[Prénom]] = first name
- [[Date de naissance (AAAA-MM-JJ)]] = date of birth (year-month-day)
- [[Adresse]], [[Code postal]] = address, postal code
- [[Téléphone]], [[Courriel]] = phone, email. In Québec, [[courriel]] is the standard word; in France, people often say [[e-mail]] or [[mail]].
- [[Disponibilités]] = when you are available

Age is often asked with the date of birth instead of [[Âge]]. And on the phone, people may ask [[C'est quoi, votre numéro ?]], a very common spoken way to ask “What's your number?”

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Focus on the liaisons and on the difference between ils sont and ils ont.

steps.intro: Put the whole unit together: numbers, dates, time and avoir.

blocks.prompt: You call a French school to register. Greet the person, say and spell your name, give your nationality and city, your age, your phone number, and ask for an appointment on a day and time that suit you.
checklist: Je suis + nationality, J'habite à + city
J'ai besoin d'un rendez-vous + day + time

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Raj Patel : P-A-T-E-L. Je suis indien et j'habite à Toronto. J'ai trente-deux ans. Mon numéro de téléphone, c'est le quatre, un, six, cinq, cinq, cinq, douze, quatre-vingt-dix-huit. J'ai besoin d'un rendez-vous pour le cours de français. Mardi, à quatorze heures, c'est possible ?
models.en: Hello! My name is Raj Patel: P-A-T-E-L. I'm Indian and I live in Toronto. I'm 32. My phone number is 416-555-1298. I need an appointment for the French class. Is Tuesday at 2 p.m. possible?

summary:
- Conjugate **avoir** in the present: [[j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont]]
- Give your age with avoir: [[J'ai trente-deux ans.]] and ask [[Tu as quel âge ? / Vous avez quel âge ?]]
- Say what you need: [[J'ai besoin d'aide.]], [[J'ai besoin d'un formulaire.]]
- Combine Units 1–3 to register: name, nationality, city, age, phone number, day and time
